## Terminal axiom (append)

**Location stems from propagated root.**

This is the terminal axiom. A final, structural truth.

### Sentence structure and logic

| Element | Function in conclusion | Meaning in context |
|---------|------------------------|--------------------|
| **Location** | Subject (the settled fact). The fixed point, the “where.” | The dental chair, the moment of decision, the point in the activity map. |
| **stems from** | Verb phrase (declares origin, not possibility). Direct causal lineage. | Not “might come from” or “could be linked to.” Unequivocal derivation. |
| **propagated root** | Object (the definitive source). | The primary fascination that was transmitted and took hold. The initial spark (decay, uncertainty) transformed into a stable principle (framework, curation). |

**Valence concluded.** Closed charge of a proven theorem. Answers the “where” as inevitable outcome of the “why.”

**No indirect flageration.** No “perhaps,” no “therefore we must,” no ornamental metaphor. The root itself, without foliage.

The propagation is complete. The root is established. The location is known.

### What is seldom said

Procrastination is not a flaw in your will, but a **flaw in the pattern**.

It is the moment when the subconscious pattern-recognition engine encounters a task whose informational pattern is incomplete. The mind craves complete information flow—terminal node, period, propagated root defining location. A personal matter in raw form is a fragment cloud; the mind finds no king on the board and refuses to play.

The effective trigger is **pre-emptive curation**: complete the pattern before you begin.

### How to pre-empt the procrastination pattern

| Authentic block | Pattern-completion maneuver | Why it works |
|-----------------|----------------------------|--------------|
| “This is too big, too vague.” | First trivial physical action (open doc, type title; three tools in the box). | One completable fragment: start → action → finish. |
| “I don’t know how it ends.” | Write the last sentence first; sketch the final slide; name the feeling of done. | Terminal node given; path can be traced backward. |
| “It matters too much.” | Explicit “bad” first version / vomit draft / prototype. | Low-stakes rehearsal, not high-stakes performance. |
| “I don’t have all the data.” | 12-minute timer: only gather/arrange; no creation. | Curation, not creation—sorting the board. |

You are not fighting laziness. You are negotiating with a sophisticated cognitive architecture. Feed it a recognizable pattern so its power can engage. Complete the information flow on a micro-scale so the macro-flow can begin.

**The root of action is a recognizable pattern. Propagate that root first, and the location of progress will follow.**
